name: Java
one_liner: A free, giant reference collection of classic computer-science algorithms written out in Java, meant for students to learn from, not for running in a real product.
buyer: No real buyer — this is a free educational reference with essentially no standalone commercial value; at best a tutor or bootcamp borrows from it for teaching material.
business_use_cases: A coding bootcamp or tutor uses its examples as free supplementary teaching material when explaining algorithms to students.
An interview-prep content creator references its implementations when building paid 'coding interview' course material.
A student uses it as a study companion while preparing for technical interviews.

money_ideas.idea: Wrap curated excerpts from it into a paid interview-prep course or flashcard app

steal_this: Honestly, this is a learning resource, not a business opportunity — the only reasonable weekend project is using it as raw material inside a paid coding-interview-prep product, and even that is a stretch.
